prompt.brief: Design a Top-K ranking system that continuously tracks changing item scores and serves the best K items quickly for use cases such as App Store rankings, Amazon bestsellers, or trending content.
successSignals: Define the ranking window, score freshness, tie-breaking, and what consistency users need from a result.
Separate fast candidate updates from the read-optimized Top-K materialization and explain when a heap is insufficient.
Handle hot keys, high-cardinality partitions, late events, score corrections, and ties without unbounded rescans.
Keep experimentation, historical analytics, and full result exports asynchronous to protect the serving path.

functional: Ingest score events for items, such as installs, sales, votes, views, or weighted engagement.
Return the Top-K items for a named scope, category, region, or time window with scores and rank positions.
Refresh rankings as events arrive and expose the observed timestamp and ranking version.
Support item eligibility, suppression, deletion, score corrections, and deterministic tie-breaking.
nonFunctional: Target p95 under 100 ms for a cached Top-K read and under 2 seconds for normal score-to-ranking freshness.
Do not lose accepted score events; consumers must be idempotent under at-least-once delivery.
Serve predictable results during bursts, hot categories, large K values, and partial worker or cache failures.
A ranking projection may be eventually consistent, but its window, version, freshness, and fallback behavior must be explicit.
scaleAssumptions: 100 million eligible items, 10,000 ranking scopes, and 1 million score events per second at peak.
Most reads request K <= 100, while a small number of export clients request larger pages through an asynchronous job.
Rankings include hourly, daily, and rolling-7-day windows; event volume and score distributions vary significantly by scope.
Retain raw events for replay and auditing, but keep serving state bounded to active items and configured windows.

metrics.label: Peak event rate
metrics.description: Score updates arrive in bursts; partition ingestion by scope and item while isolating hot scopes.

metrics.label: Serving latency
metrics.description: Read a precomputed Top-K snapshot instead of sorting all eligible items per request.

metrics.label: Ranking freshness
metrics.description: The target for ordinary scopes; return version and observedAt when a projection is behind.

metrics.label: Default K
metrics.description: Bound the synchronous response and route large result sets through paginated or asynchronous exports.

entities.name: ScoreEvent
entities.notes: An immutable event is deduplicated by event_id and retained long enough to replay windows or correct late data.

entities.name: ItemScore
entities.notes: A materialized score for one scope and window; update semantics must distinguish additive metrics from replacement corrections.

entities.name: RankingSnapshot
entities.notes: The serving contract is a versioned bounded snapshot, not an implicit promise that every event has already arrived.

entities.name: RankingRule
entities.notes: Version rules so a replay or experiment can explain why an item received its rank.

apis.contract: { eventId, scopeId, itemId, delta, eventTime } -> { accepted, sequence }
apis.notes: Authenticate the producer, validate scope and item eligibility, and deduplicate eventId before publishing to the stream.

apis.contract: { items[], k, version, generatedAt, watermark, stale }
apis.notes: Serve a bounded snapshot from cache; reject unbounded K and include freshness metadata for clients.
Look up an item's rank from a rank index or bounded neighbor structure; do not scan the full Top-K list.

apis.contract: { scopeId, window, k, asOf? } -> { jobId, status }
apis.notes: Route large K, historical as-of queries, and exports to an asynchronous snapshot job with progress and quota controls.

dataFlow.title: Accept a score event
dataFlow.description: The ingestion API validates the producer, item, scope, timestamp, and event ID, then appends the event to a durable partitioned stream.

dataFlow.title: Update candidate scores
dataFlow.description: Windowed aggregators consume events idempotently, apply the versioned scoring rule, expire old contributions, and write bounded candidate state.

dataFlow.title: Maintain the Top-K
dataFlow.description: A ranking worker merges candidate updates into a per-scope data structure, evicts items below the boundary, resolves ties deterministically, and advances a watermark.

dataFlow.title: Publish a ranking snapshot
dataFlow.description: The worker atomically publishes a versioned snapshot to the serving cache and emits invalidation or update signals without blocking event ingestion.

dataFlow.title: Serve or rebuild asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Reads return the newest acceptable snapshot with freshness metadata; large K, historical queries, replay, and experiments run as isolated background jobs.

architecture.title: Top-K ranking reference architecture
architecture.summary: Durable score events feed windowed candidate state and a per-scope Top-K projector; versioned snapshots make reads fast while replay and watermarks make eventual consistency visible and repairable.

layers.label: Serving layer
layers.description: Clients request bounded, freshness-aware ranking snapshots and item rank lookups.

layers.label: Ingestion and state layer
layers.description: Producers append score events while windowed aggregators maintain candidate scores.

layers.label: Ranking projection layer
layers.description: Partition owners maintain Top-K structures and publish atomic snapshots per scope and window.

layers.label: Replay and operations
layers.description: Historical replay, exports, analytics, and observability stay off the synchronous serving path.

keyPaths.label: Event ingestion path
keyPaths.description: Producer -> event API -> durable stream -> windowed score aggregation.

keyPaths.label: Ranking serving path
keyPaths.description: Client -> ranking API -> snapshot cache/store -> bounded Top-K response.

keyPaths.label: Projection path
keyPaths.description: Candidate state -> per-scope Top-K projector -> versioned snapshot publication.

components.label: Ranking clients
components.description: Request Top-K snapshots, show freshness, and use bounded pagination or job status for large results.

components.label: Edge gateway
components.description: Authenticates producers and readers, applies quotas, and routes requests by scope key.

components.label: Score event API
components.description: Validates event shape, timestamps, eligibility, and producer permissions before durable append.

components.label: Score event stream
components.description: Durably retains partitioned events for aggregation, replay, analytics, and correction workflows.

components.label: Ranking rules
components.description: Stores versioned weights, windows, eligibility policies, and deterministic tie-break rules.

components.label: Windowed aggregators
components.description: Deduplicate events, apply score rules, handle late data, and maintain candidate score state by scope and window.

components.label: Candidate score store
components.description: Stores bounded active scores and indexes candidates near each scope's ranking boundary.

components.label: Top-K projector
components.description: Maintains heaps or ordered sets per scope shard, merges hot-scope shards, and advances ranking versions.

components.label: Ranking snapshots
components.description: Persists versioned bounded snapshots for warm recovery, auditing, and cache refill.

components.label: Serving cache
components.description: Serves recent snapshots with stale markers, stampede protection, and scope-aware TTLs.

components.label: Ranking API
components.description: Returns bounded snapshots and item rank lookups, enforcing K limits and freshness policy.

components.label: Replay and repair jobs
components.description: Rebuilds windows from retained events, validates score corrections, and repairs projection drift in a shadow path.

components.label: Large-query jobs
components.description: Runs large K, historical, and export requests asynchronously with quotas and progress tracking.

components.label: Analytics and experiments
components.description: Consumes events and snapshots for trends, offline evaluation, and ranking experiments without affecting serving latency.

components.label: Ranking observability
components.description: Tracks event lag, watermark age, boundary churn, cache hit rate, projection drift, and hot-scope saturation.

connections.label: Read / submit
connections.description: Authenticated ranking reads and producer event requests.

connections.label: Score event
connections.description: Routes validated producer events to ingestion.

connections.label: Durable append
connections.description: Appends deduplicatable events before downstream processing.

connections.label: Rule revision
connections.description: Workers apply the correct versioned scoring rule.

connections.label: Window events
connections.description: At-least-once consumption with event dedupe and watermarks.

connections.label: Candidate scores
connections.description: Writes windowed scores and boundary candidate indexes.

connections.label: Score changes
connections.description: Feeds scope owners with changed candidates and boundary updates.

connections.label: Versioned Top-K
connections.description: Publishes an atomic snapshot with watermark and generatedAt.

connections.label: Cache refill
connections.description: Warms serving cache and provides recovery after eviction.

connections.label: Bounded query
connections.description: Routes scope/window/K requests to the serving API.

connections.label: Snapshot read
connections.description: Returns the newest acceptable snapshot within the freshness policy.

connections.label: Recovery read
connections.description: Refills or serves when cache state is missing.

connections.label: Top-K response
connections.description: Returns entries, score, rank, version, and freshness metadata.

connections.label: Replay input
connections.description: Rebuilds historical windows and validates corrections asynchronously.

connections.label: Async events
connections.description: Supports experiments and reports without blocking ranking updates.

deepDives.title: Maintaining Top-K efficiently
points: For a bounded K, a min-heap can retain the current winners, but updates need a map from item to heap position or lazy deletion to avoid stale entries.
Keep a candidate buffer around the K boundary because an item just below the cutoff can enter after a score update; a fixed periodic full scan is a recovery path, not the normal request path.
For high-cardinality or highly skewed scopes, shard candidates, compute local Top-K, and merge local winners with enough boundary slack to preserve correctness.

deepDives.title: Windows, late events, and corrections
points: Use event-time windows with watermarks and a lateness policy; state clearly when a late event can revise a published ranking.
Treat score replacements and corrections as versioned operations, not blindly additive deltas, and deduplicate event IDs before applying them.
Publish a new ranking version after correction and expose observedAt so consumers can distinguish a fresh correction from an older snapshot.

deepDives.title: Hot scopes and serving resilience
points: Partition event processing and snapshot publication for hot scopes, then isolate their queues and cache keys from ordinary scopes.
Cache immutable versioned snapshots with stampede protection; a stale-but-labeled snapshot is preferable to sorting millions of items synchronously.
Bound K and use asynchronous jobs for large exports, historical as-of queries, and full rank lists.

deepDives.title: Explainability and ranking evolution
points: Store rule revision, score components, watermark, and tie-breaker in the snapshot so a rank can be explained and reproduced.
Keep raw events and projection versions for replay, offline evaluation, and A/B tests without changing the serving contract.
Apply eligibility and suppression at both aggregation and serving boundaries because moderation or catalog state can change after an event arrives.

tradeoffs.title: Exact Top-K versus approximate ranking
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use exact per-scope Top-K for normal bounded K with candidate boundaries, and explicitly offer approximate sketches only when cardinality or throughput makes exact maintenance too expensive.
tradeoffs.caution: An approximate answer without an error bound or freshness label is difficult to productize; exact rescans per request fail at scale.

tradeoffs.title: Streaming updates versus periodic batch
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use streaming aggregation for freshness and periodic batch or replay jobs for correction, reconciliation, and historical windows.
tradeoffs.caution: Streaming state is operationally complex, while batch-only ranking creates visible staleness and synchronized compute spikes.

tradeoffs.title: Push snapshots versus pull reads
tradeoffs.recommendation: Publish immutable snapshots to a cache and let clients pull bounded results; optionally send invalidation hints for live dashboards.
tradeoffs.caution: Pushing every rank change to every viewer multiplies fanout and creates unnecessary coupling between computation and presentation.

commonMistakes: Sorting every eligible item synchronously for every Top-K request.
Using a single global heap without scope partitioning, hot-key protection, or recovery semantics.
Ignoring event-time windows, late events, duplicate messages, score corrections, and deterministic ties.
Returning a ranking without version, watermark, generatedAt, or a stale/freshness contract.
Allowing unlimited K and running exports, historical queries, or analytics on the serving path.

followUps.question: How would you return an item's rank when it is not in the Top-K?
followUps.answer: Maintain a bounded rank index or score distribution near the requested item, or run an asynchronous rank job for arbitrary positions; do not scan the full population on a latency-sensitive request.

followUps.question: How would you support a personalized Top-K per user?
followUps.answer: Generate bounded candidates from user or segment signals, then rank them with a versioned feature snapshot; cache by user and rule revision with strict privacy and cost limits.

followUps.question: What happens when the ranking worker fails?
followUps.answer: Continue serving the last acceptable immutable snapshot with a stale marker, replay retained events into a shadow projector, compare versions, and switch after validation.

followUps.question: How do you validate that a heap implementation is correct?
followUps.answer: Periodically compare sampled scopes against an offline full sort, monitor boundary churn and score gaps, and use deterministic tie-breaks so discrepancies are reproducible.

rubric.description: The answer defines K, scope, window, event time, ties, eligibility, freshness, and whether results are exact or approximate.
The design explains bounded heaps or ordered structures, candidate boundaries, shard merging, and update/deletion behavior.
The architecture handles high event rates, hot scopes, cache reads, bounded K, and asynchronous large queries.
Idempotency, late events, corrections, replay, watermarks, versioned snapshots, and reconciliation are explicit.
The response includes stale fallback, lag and drift metrics, rule revisions, explainability, and safe ranking evolution.
